title: Composition comparison with normalized representative formulas
statement: Given normalized lifts lf, lg and lk, and a specified geometric isomorphism from the inverse image of k to that of the path g then f commuting with structural ring maps, there are ordinary and derived pullback composition isomorphisms, with scalar-insertion and flat-term K-flat representative formulas, and tensor/unit compatibility. The ordinary right comparison is its ordinary adjunction mate. The derived adjunction mate of the left comparison satisfies the right-derived-unit composition formula at every complex. Identity, general 2-isomorphism transport and existence of lifts are not asserted. The recorded presentations, edges, representative models and normalization equations are those defined in [def-sfb-ringed-derived-comparison-data].

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition) and 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility); original comparison proof steps 3–9

proof.text: 1. Transport the geometric right-adjoint mate through the normalized underlying sheaf isomorphisms. Generalized scalar-linear combinations and the structural ring-map equation show that it and its inverse are module maps. Assemble the resulting natural module isomorphism, conjugate the normalized module adjunctions, and apply their underlying Hom formulas to obtain the ordinary scalar-insertion equation.

2. Choose a normalized lift of the identity geometric morphism using the adjoint and tensor lift existence theorems, and use its identity comparison. The ordinary composition comparison and this identity comparison define a ringed tensor square. Apply the existing derived square comparison and cancel the derived identity comparison. Its representative equation gives precisely the composition alpha formula.

3. The representative square tensor compatibility descends to all derived pairs by full faithfulness of restriction to the resolving homotopy subcategory. The tensor model normalization identifies all recorded representative models at the same site. Cancel the identity comparison using its tensor compatibility. For an invertible transformation between strong monoidal functors, tensor compatibility implies unit compatibility by left unitality and faithfulness of tensoring with the image of the tensor unit.

4. Extend the canonical inverse Hom formula from K-injective targets to every target by a K-injective resolution, naturality of eta, and cancellation of the localized resolution. Resolve the ordinary k-pushforward of each complex by a flat-term K-flat complex. After precomposition with its invertible localization and transposition across the composite derived adjunction, both sides of kappa_model become the canonical inverse Hom formulas. The complexwise ordinary mate equation and the derived alpha composition equation identify these transposes, hence the original right-mate equation.
